title: ～のが下手だ — being bad at doing something
summary: Verb (dictionary form) + のが下手です means ‘I am bad at ～ing’. The の turns the verb into a noun, and 下手 is a な-adjective. It is used for skills and activities.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形＋のが下手だ
patterns.gloss: dictionary form + のが下手だ (歌うのが下手)
noun + が下手だ (歌が下手)

body.p: Put the verb in the dictionary form, add の to make it a noun phrase, then が下手です: 泳ぐのが下手です. The thing you are weak at is marked with が, not を.
Talk about your own weakness or someone else's. For other people it can sound blunt, so it is used mostly about yourself or in plain description.
The opposite is ～のが上手です (good at ～ing). Both are な-adjectives, so the past is 下手でした.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）は歌（うた）うのが下手（へた）です。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa utau no ga heta desu.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）は絵（え）をかくのが下手（へた）です。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa e o kaku no ga heta desu.
examples.tr: I am bad at drawing pictures.
examples.note: The object 絵を stays inside the verb phrase.

examples.ja: 弟（おとうと）は泳（およ）ぐのが下手（へた）です。
examples.romaji: Otōto wa oyogu no ga heta desu.
examples.tr: My younger brother is bad at swimming.

pitfalls: Use が, not を, before 下手: 歌うのが下手です.
The verb before の must be in the dictionary (plain) form, not the ます form.
